name: Midjourney
summary: The image model people still judge by aesthetically, sold as a subscription with no official public API.
description:
Midjourney's output has a look, and that is the product: for concept art, editorial illustration, moodboards and anything where taste matters more than literal prompt compliance, it still sets the bar that other models get compared against. Version-to-version improvements have been about coherence and text rendering rather than novelty, which suits paying users.

Two structural frictions: there is no first-party public API, so production pipelines mean automating the web app or not shipping it, and the training-data posture has kept enterprise adoption cautious. If you need exact brand control or reproducible character consistency, this is a beautiful tool pointed at the wrong job.
